faq.title: The questions we get asked most
faq.subtitle: We answer the important questions about work, timelines and the process.

items.q: Do I need to come to your office?
items.a: No. We do most projects entirely online: we have calls, discuss the layout, send materials and agree on decisions remotely.

items.q: Do you work with small apartments?
items.a: Yes. For small apartments a thoughtful layout matters even more — we help you use every square meter.

items.q: How long does a design project take?
items.a: On average from 14 to 25 days depending on the format and area. The exact timeline is fixed in the contract.

items.q: Can I order just the layout without visualization?
items.a: Yes, the "Layout" format is a separate package. Visualization can be added later.
Support during implementation: advising the contractor, checking compliance with the project and answering questions as the renovation goes.

items.q: How is the project paid for?
items.a: We work under a contract. Payment is split into stages — without full prepayment at the start.

items.q: What if I don't like the result?
items.a: We agree on the concept step by step: you see and approve decisions before the finale, so there are no surprises.

faq.q: How is a layout different from a full project?
faq.a: The layout solves function and arrangement. A full project adds visualizations, materials and concept plans.
Yes, visualization and other services can be added as a separate stage.

faq.q: How closely will the visualization match the result?
faq.a: We pick real materials and furniture, so the result is as close to the visualization as possible.

faq.q: How many angles do you make?
faq.a: Usually 2–3 angles per key room; the count is discussed per project.

sketch.subtitle: The ideal format to start a renovation without overpaying: layout, concept and key schemes.
sketch.intro: A concept project gives you everything for a confident renovation: a thoughtful layout, a visual concept and concept plans for furniture, light and sockets.

faq.q: Is a concept project enough for contractors?
faq.a: Yes, the concept plans are enough for the crew to understand the key project decisions.

faq.q: How is a concept project different from a working one?
faq.a: The concept project fixes the concept and key schemes; working documentation is more detailed drawings for complex solutions.
